A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SlowBA, and their main text, equations, figures and tables are readable. v1 includes Appendices A-G; v3 moves the prompt and reward-parameter study into the main text but refers to supplementary implementation and case-study material that is not supplied. This limits comparison of appendix-only content.

before.justification: v1 reports original GUI-R1 experiments, ablations, defense evaluations, a human trigger assessment and a train-ticket case study, with additional results in its appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds clean-data retraining and inference-setting evaluations in Tables 4 and 6.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1-4.5 retain the same pop-up construction, long-response SFT, trigger-conditioned reward and GRPO optimization. The prompt shown in v3 Section 4.4 already appears in v1 Appendix A; it does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use OmniAct-Web, GUI-Act-Web, ScreenSpot-Pro and AndroidControl-Low, alongside the human trigger assessment and train-ticket scenario. The added retraining and inference-setting experiments establish no new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The Gaussian Noise, JPEG compression, Verbose Image and VisualTrap attack comparators are unchanged. The defense comparison adds a Re-train method in v3 Table 4, absent from v1 Table 3, while retaining the existing defenses.

E3.justification: v3 adds retraining on another clean dataset, described as avoiding data leakage, and an inference study crossing maximum lengths of 2048 and 8192 with temperatures of 0.0 and 0.5. These are additional evaluation settings; the retained main experiments show no reported protocol revision.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of robustness to clean-data retraining and sensitivity to inference length and temperature. The two-stage ablation and other matched analyses remain unchanged; the alpha/beta study moves from v1 Appendix B to v3 Table 1. Additional appendix cases cannot be checked against the unavailable v3 supplement.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean scores and retain the same Fleiss' kappa agreement reporting for the human study. Neither supplied PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark, ablation, scaling, module and reward-parameter results are numerically unchanged. v3 adds Re-train results of 275.36% I-length, 61.37% I-latency, 59.74% I-energy and triggered/clean accuracies of 54.4/64.7. Table 6 reports 49.18/66.92 at temperature 0.0 and 41.84/65.18 at 0.5 for lengths 2048/8192; its metric and units are implicit in the latency discussion. Appendix-only results remain incompletely comparable.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions and Equations (1)-(5) match. v1 Appendix C additionally discusses GRPO mathematics, including a U-statistic/oracle-gradient assertion. Its later counterpart is unavailable, so retention or revision of this appendix-only mathematical material cannot be established.

C1.justification: The abstract and three main contributions retain the same efficiency-backdoor claim, two-stage RBI strategy, realistic pop-up triggers and accuracy-preservation claims. The added concluding emphasis on responsiveness reiterates the existing motivation rather than redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: v3 Section 5.6 adds the interpretation that the latency effect is not strongly tied to particular inference settings, citing shorter maximum lengths and different temperatures. The existing mechanism explanations and principal applicability claims remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: The hardware, training frameworks, poisoning ratios and code-access disclosure remain unchanged, and the Stage I prompt is relocated. v1 supplies exact training hyperparameters and accuracy rules, including the 140-pixel and F1 thresholds, that are absent from the supplied v3. Because v3 redirects implementation details to unavailable supplementary material, their retention or revision cannot be determined.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including GEM, Verios, GUI-AIMA, RegionMarker and VLM personalization work, while dropping MuseLLM, the Qwen2.5-VL web reference and the train-ticket news source. The research positioning remains substantially the same. Publication updates to retained references do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording and author-information edits, converts related-work subsections to paragraph headings, and combines the mechanism and case-study sections under Qualitative Results. It integrates existing appendix material into the method section and adds acknowledgements; most prose and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the inference-settings table, expands the defense table with a retraining row, and relocates the existing reward-parameter table into the main text. Existing figures and tables are repositioned, and Figure 6 changes its description from attention to importance. The main figure artwork and overall visual design remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful additional retraining and inference-sensitivity evidence and makes existing method details easier to find. However, its unavailable supplement prevents checking the training details, accuracy rules and supporting cases supplied with v1. The new inference table also leaves its metric and units implicit, and the retraining procedure is sparsely specified. These gaps prevent a reliable judgment of the net overall quality change.
